answers:
I found 13 problems across the three new files, numbered below. I checked them against your `.code-standards/` rules, ruff and lizard. I couldn't run oxlint because it isn't installed locally, so the TSX file was reviewed by hand only.

### `app/api/loyalty_routes.py`
1. **`app/api/loyalty_routes.py:10`**: `os.environ.get("LOYALTY_RATE", ...)` breaks your `cs-env-outside-config` rule (severity error). Only `app/config.py` should read the environment. Add a `loyalty_rate: float` field to `Settings` and read it from `settings`. As written, a bad value is only caught when someone requests this page, not at startup.
2. **`app/api/loyalty_routes.py:11`**: The handler calls `get_db().fetch_one(...)` directly. Your `std-routes-delegate` standard says to pass `get_db()` through to the service instead.
3. **`app/api/loyalty_routes.py:12-13`**: A missing customer gets `{"points": 0}` with a 200 status. It should be a 404, which you get by having the service raise `LookupError`. Right now a wrong ID looks the same as a real customer with no points.
4. **`app/api/loyalty_routes.py:14-15`**: The handler decides the gold tier rate itself, which is business logic and also breaks `std-routes-delegate`. Worse, `points_for` already gives gold a +50 bonus and no cap (`loyalty_service.py:16-17, 32`). The tier rules end up split across two layers, and any other caller of `points_for` (such as a job) won't double the rate, so it will compute different points.
5. **`app/api/loyalty_routes.py`**: The route is never registered. `app/main.py:1-4` imports each route module so its routes get registered, and `loyalty_routes` isn't in that list, so the endpoint doesn't exist at runtime.

### `app/services/loyalty_service.py`
6. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:1`**: `import json` is unused (ruff F401).
7. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:6-10`**: `find_customer` is never called. It returns `None` for a missing record, which breaks `std-service-errors` (it should raise `LookupError(f"customer {customer_id} not found")`). The `if row is None: return None; return row` is also redundant. `customer_service.get_customer` already does this lookup properly, so use that instead.
8. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:13-34`**: `points_for` has a cyclomatic complexity of 11, above your threshold of 10 (per lizard). Table lookups would simplify it, for example `TIER_BONUS = {"gold": 50, "silver": 20, "bronze": 5}`.
9. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:13`**: The function takes a raw `dict` instead of the `Customer` model the other services use. It reads fields `Customer` may not have (`spent_cents`, `birthday_month`, `referrals`, `newsletter`, `blocked`) through `.get()` with silent defaults, so a misspelled column name gives wrong points instead of an error.
10. **`app/services/loyalty_service.py:30-33`**: Several things are hard to follow here:
    - Blocked customers get their whole score computed and then zeroed. Returning early would be clearer.
    - `1000`, `50`, `20`, `10`, `25`, `5` and `3` are unnamed numbers mixed into the logic.
    - Line 22 adds the birthday bonus whenever `birthday_month` is set at all, not when it's the current month. That's probably a bug.

### `web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx`
11. **`web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx:6`**: The component calls `fetch` directly, which breaks `std-components-use-api-modules`. Add `getLoyalty(customerId)` to a `web/src/api/loyalty.ts` module that uses `apiClient`. As written, it also has no `r.ok` check and no `.catch`: an error response gives `setPoints(undefined)` and shows "undefined pts", and a network error is an unhandled rejection.
12. **`web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx:10`**: A leftover `debugger;` statement runs on every render.
13. **`web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx:14-25`**: `summarize` has nothing to do with the badge and is the third copy of the same function (also in `OrderList.tsx:24` and `InvoiceList.tsx:24`). Your duplication check would flag it. Move one copy into `web/src/lib/`, and use the existing `formatCents` in `web/src/lib/format.ts` instead of `(cents / 100).toFixed(2)`. This file also exports it, unlike the private copies in the other two.
